summary: Defines a new BGP encoding that lets routers share traffic flow specifications, which are rules matching particular kinds of traffic, such as by destination prefix and other packet fields. This lets the routing system spread finer-grained filtering information than a plain destination prefix, often to help block unwanted traffic. It was replaced by RFC 8955.

eli5.summary: Normally a road sign says only which town a road leads to. This adds extra signs such as which kinds of trucks to stop, and passes them to every nearby road.

questions: how to distribute traffic filter rules with bgp
how does bgp flow specification work
how to block ddos traffic with bgp
what are flow specification component types
subtitle: Using BGP to spread fine-grained traffic filtering rules, mainly to fight denial-of-service attacks.

tldr.problem: Operators who fight denial-of-service attacks often advertise a unicast route for the attacked prefix, which can only match a destination prefix and mixes filtering data with routing data.
tldr.mechanism: A new BGP NLRI type encodes a flow specification: a set of match components such as prefixes, protocol, ports and packet length. Extended communities say what to do with matching traffic, and a validation step checks the rule against unicast routing.
tldr.outcome: The rules ride on existing BGP sessions and policy. RFC 5575 has been obsoleted by RFC 8955.

today: RFC 5575 is a Proposed Standard that has been obsoleted by RFC 8955, and it was also updated by RFC 7674. Read RFC 8955 for the current specification.

sections.title: Why Distribute Flow Rules with BGP
sections.content:
Routers can already classify, rate limit, filter or redirect packets using rules that match several header fields. A flow specification is such a set of matching criteria, for example source and destination prefixes, IP protocol and port numbers. This RFC defines how to encode one as a BGP NLRI (Network Layer Reachability Information) so that it can be distributed like routing data.

The immediate problem is (distributed) denial-of-service attacks. A common technique is to inject a unicast route for the prefix under attack, perhaps marked with a community that turns into a discard next hop. The RFC lists two drawbacks: only destination prefixes can be matched, and filtering information is mixed with routing information. BGP is chosen because it already offers point-to-multipoint distribution, inter-domain policy and a way to check rules against unicast routing. The RFC also says operators should keep the amount of information below device limits.
sections.eli5: When a website is flooded with junk traffic, the old way is to block the whole street. This lets you block just the junk trucks and let everyone else through.

sections.title: The Flow Specification NLRI
sections.content:
The NLRI travels in the MP_REACH_NLRI and MP_UNREACH_NLRI attributes of RFC 4760. It starts with a length of 1 or 2 octets: values below 240 use one octet, and larger values use two octets whose first nibble is all ones, up to a maximum of 4095. If the application needs no next hop, a 0-octet next hop is used and ignored on receipt. Both ends MUST negotiate the Multiprotocol Extension Capability (Code 1) for the (AFI, SAFI) pair in use.

The value is a list of optional components. A packet matches when it matches the intersection (AND) of all components present. Components MUST appear in increasing type order. Types 1 and 2 are destination and source prefixes. The others (protocol, ports, ICMP type and code, TCP flags, packet length, DSCP and fragment) are lists of operator and value pairs. Each operator byte has an end-of-list bit, an AND bit, a length field and less-than, greater-than and equal bits, which can be combined to make comparisons such as at-least or not-equal. If a receiver does not know a component type, it cannot use the rule for filtering but should still propagate it.

For example, the rule for all packets to 10.0.1/24 and TCP port 25 is encoded as 0x01 18 0a 00 01 for the destination, 03 81 06 for the protocol and 04 81 19 for the port.
sections.eli5: A rule is like a checklist: the destination is this house, the vehicle is a truck, and it is going to this door. A packet is only stopped if it ticks every box on the list.

sections.title: Rule Ordering and Validation
sections.content:
More than one rule can match a flow, so the order must not depend on arrival order and must be the same across the network. Rules are compared component by component from the left. The rule with the lowest type value at the first difference wins. For prefixes, the lowest value of the common prefix length wins, and if those are equal the more specific prefix wins. Other components are compared as binary strings with memcmp(), and the longer string wins when the shorter one is a prefix of it.

A flow rule received from a peer is feasible only if two checks pass. First, its originator MUST match the originator of the best-match unicast route for the destination prefix in the rule. Second, no more specific unicast route may have been received from a different neighboring AS. The idea is that the neighbor that is the next destination for the traffic may ask for it to be dropped. An eBGP implementation MUST also check that the neighboring AS is leftmost in the AS_PATH, which the base BGP specification leaves optional.
sections.eli5: When two rules both apply, there is a fixed tie-break so every router picks the same one. A router also only believes a rule from the neighbor who is actually responsible for that road.

sections.title: Actions, SAFIs and VPNs
sections.content:
The default action for a matching flow is to accept it. Four extended communities, of the type described in RFC 4360, give standard actions: traffic-rate (0x8006), traffic-action (0x8007), redirect (0x8008, which sends traffic to a VRF chosen by Route Target) and traffic-marking (0x8009, which rewrites the DSCP value). A traffic rate of 0 means all matching traffic is discarded. The traffic-action community has a Terminal Action bit (bit 47), which lets later rules also apply when set, and a Sample bit (bit 46) for sampling and logging. The list is not meant to be complete, and other actions can be mapped from user-defined communities.

For the Internet case the RFC uses (AFI=1, SAFI=133). For BGP/MPLS VPNs it adds (AFI=1, SAFI=134), where the NLRI is an 8-byte Route Distinguisher followed by the flow specification, and Route Targets control propagation. Rules from remote PE routers are accepted by default in that case. Implementations SHOULD provide a way to log filtered packet headers and to count matches per rule.
sections.eli5: Once a rule matches, a label says what to do: let it through slowly, throw it away, send it down a side road, or stamp it with a priority mark.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Inter-provider routing is a web of trust: neighbors are trusted to advertise valid reachability. As long as filtering rules are restricted to match the corresponding unicast routing paths, the RFC says the security properties equal those of existing BGP unicast routing. Where they are not, the door opens to further denial-of-service attacks, which is why validation matters.

The RFC also warns that firewall-like rules in routers without central management can make failures hard to diagnose. For example, a rule could allow TCP but not ICMP, or let packets smaller than 900 or larger than 1000 bytes through but not those in between. Such capabilities should be used with care. When automated systems originate the rules, their correctness and the rate of advertisement should be limited.
sections.eli5: A rule that blocks traffic is powerful, so a router only obeys it if it comes from the right neighbor. Odd rules can also confuse the people who run the network.

items.label: Port
items.desc: Matches source or destination TCP/UDP port.

items.label: Packet length
items.desc: Total IP packet length, including the IP header.

items.label: traffic-rate
items.desc: Rate in bytes per second; 0 discards all matching traffic.

items.label: traffic-action
items.desc: Bitmask with Terminal Action and Sample bits.

items.label: redirect
items.desc: Redirects to a VRF by Route Target.
